summary: A quieter news day for supplements, so today leans on sleep science and caffeine. Sleep regularity (going to bed and waking at the same time) is showing up across this month's research, an American Heart Association abstract on energy drinks has put caffeine milligrams in the news, and Maharashtra FDA's 13 Nov seizure of unapproved nutraceuticals is the freshest Indian enforcement story. Reddit could not be read live today (the built-in browser blocks reddit.com), so subreddit picks rely on news and our own Instagram.

trends.topic: Sleep regularity matters as much as hours (UK Biobank: 38% lower depression risk, 33% lower anxiety risk in regular sleepers)
trends.angle: Nights: a same-time-every-night ritual. Observational data, so no causal claims.

trends.topic: AHA preliminary study (2 Nov): energy drinks and stimulant products over-represented in FDA heart adverse event reports, 45% in 18 to 34 year olds
trends.angle: Mornings: count caffeine in mg. 80 mg per stick against the 400 mg daily figure regulators cite. Industry groups dispute the method; never use fear.

trends.topic: Maharashtra FDA seizes Rs 1.39 crore of unapproved nutraceuticals across 17 sites in one day (13 Nov)
trends.angle: Both: a buyer's checklist (FSSAI licence, doses in mg, a readable lab report).

trends.topic: Caffeine + L-theanine: 2026 athlete crossover trial finds no extra physical performance benefit
trends.angle: Mornings, education only: the evidence for the pair is about focus and smoother energy, not strength. Keeps our claims honest.

trends.topic: Workforce Health Index 2026 (Loop Health): high stress among urban professionals up from 33.9% to 40.4%; short sleep in 41% of high-stress responses
trends.angle: Both: our buyer's daily reality. Community posts, no selling. Good LinkedIn material for Monday 23 Nov.

trends.topic: ResMed survey: 71% of Indian workers say poor sleep hurts their work; 58% say workload interferes with sleep
trends.angle: Nights: supporting number for posts on desk workers and sleep.

trends.topic: MIT: gentle sounds during sleep amplify the brain's overnight cleaning waves (did not show more waste cleared)
trends.angle: Education: read past the headline. Fits our evidence-first voice.

trends.topic: 19-year study links long, frequent and morning naps in older adults to declining health
trends.angle: Education and community: what a good workday nap looks like. Older adults and association only.

trends.topic: Wearable ultrasound patch gets people into REM 43 minutes sooner (28 participants)
trends.angle: Education: sleep tech is moving fast, but the study is tiny. Possible X post later this week.

trends.topic: Independent ranking of 15 Indian supplement brands on verifiable evidence (6 Nov); flags brands that claim testing but show no report page
trends.angle: Brand: published lab reports are becoming the test buyers use. Do not name brands in public posts.

instagram: Newest reel (16 Nov) opens a nutritionist series: 'Most supplements? Wasted money. SILT keeps only what's useful', with part 2, the Skip list, promised next. The 14 Nov reel repeats the launch proof (4.9/5 on Judge.me, 250 customers, 10 repeat buyers in 15 days) and the 9 Nov fibre-gap reel with food maths is still the best performer (27 likes, 2 comments). Today's X post 4 points to the Skip list, so it should go live on Instagram this week. Comments could not be read without logging in; yesterday's open complaint about a stuck delivery under the fibre reel should still be checked.
competitors: Quiet week for Indian rivals in the news; HUL's full takeover of OZiva and USV's majority stake in Wellbeing Nutrition are the latest structural moves. Abroad, Momentous launched 117 new Meta ads in October (407 live), AG1 is pushing into retail (Vitamin Shoppe) and sport (Swansea City kit), and LMNT is suing the health-scoring app Oasis over lead claims, a sign that third-party scoring is now a battleground. An independent Indian ranking (6 Nov) scored brands on verifiable evidence and called out one that claims testing but has no report page. Borrow: make our per-ingredient lab reports easy to find from every post.
